question: Should OpenClaw accept fail-closed Codex Computer Use readiness with default shared per-agent cache reconciliation plus opt-in repair and health checks in this PR?
rationale: The code is coherent and well-proven, but the PR changes enabled-user startup behavior, local cache state, sandbox probing, and optional process repair policy, which are maintainer product/security-boundary choices rather than purely mechanical correctness questions.

options.title: Accept After Docs Fix
options.body: Update the stale readiness paragraph, then land the PR with owner acceptance of the new default cache and live-probe behavior.

options.title: Split Risky Surfaces
options.body: Land cache/live-status hardening first and defer lease manager, periodic health, or repair policy into narrower follow-up PRs.

options.title: Prefer Compatibility Default
options.body: Keep existing readiness behavior by default and require an explicit strict/readiness option before fail-closed live probes can block enabled users.

recommendation.title: Accept After Docs Fix
recommendation.body: Update the stale readiness paragraph, then land the PR with owner acceptance of the new default cache and live-probe behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the Codex Computer Use setup boundary and are the clearest historical owner for accepting the readiness contract change.
